paper_title: Adapting Whisper for Regional Dialects Enhancing Public Services for   Vulnerable Populations in the United Kingdom
caption: Difference in average word error rate (WER) from Whisper large-v3 after cumulative automated optimisation steps.
model_annotation: This horizontal bar chart illustrates the difference in average word error rate (WER) from the Whisper large-v3 baseline model after applying various cumulative automated optimisation steps, with the y-axis listing the optimisations applied in descending order of their WER impact: “Normalised” (0.00334), “Add Spacing” (0.00319), “Remove Spacing” (0.00311), “Americanisms” (0.00299), and “Dates” (0.00257). The x-axis represents the “Difference in Average WER from Whisper large,” scaled linearly from 0.000 to 0.003, with tick marks at intervals of 0.001. For each optimisation, two bars are shown side-by-side, colored orange for the “NESAC ft model” and green for the “SASHA ft model,” indicating the respective WER differences. The “Normalised” optimisation resulted in the highest WER difference for both models, with the NESAC model at 0.00334 and the SASHA model at 0.00323. The “Dates” optimisation produced the lowest WER difference, with the NESAC model at 0.00257 and the SASHA model at 0.00228. The bars are grouped by optimisation, with the orange bar consistently appearing slightly longer than the green bar for each category, indicating a higher WER difference for the NESAC model across all optimisations. The chart does not show any sorting of bars by value, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond their color coding and length.
